== Biography ==
Busio was born in Seattle, Washington. He began playing ''League of Legends'' when he was 7 years old. In 2020, he played in the amateur circuit as a mid laner for [[Polar Ace]], but swapped roles to support when he joined [[100 Thieves Next]] at the beginning of the 2021 season. As a support, Busio quickly rose through the ranks of the [[100 Thieves]] organization. He was promoted to [[100 Thieves Academy]] in the middle of 2021 and was named the most valuable academy prospect during [[NA Academy League/2022 Season/Summer Season|2022 Summer]].<ref>[https://twitter.com/PathToLCS/status/1564368922404564992 Path To LCS' Tweet] ''twitter.com''</ref>

=== 2023 Season ===
For the 2023 season, Busio was promoted to the 100 Thieves main roster to play alongside returning LCS legend [[Doublelift]].

=== 2024 Season ===
In 2024, Busio achieved greater success after joining [[FlyQuest]] to play alongside rookie [[Massu]]. A 2nd place finish in Spring playoffs birthed FlyQuest appearances at [[2024 Mid-Season Invitational]] and [[Esports World Cup 2024]]. In the Summer split, FlyQuest defeated Team Liquid in the finals for Busio's first LCS championship trophy and first qualification to Worlds.

== Trivia ==
* His father, [[wikipedia:Krzysztof Cwalina|Krzysztof Cwalina]], is a former professional swimmer who represented Poland at the 1992 Summer Olympics in Barcelona.<ref>[https://x.com/Busio/status/2049951736270320032 Busio's X Post] ''x.com''</ref>
* Reached Challenger when he was 15 years old in Season 9.
* Has dual nationality.
* His favorite pro player is [[Keria]].

=== Individual Awards ===
* NA Academy Most Valuable Prospect (2022 Summer)
* LCS 1st All-Pro Team x1 (2024 Spring)
* LCS 3rd All-Pro Team x1 (2024 Summer)
